name: Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers

ingredients.buy: 7 green bell peppers, halved and seeded
3 1/2 lb yellow onions, sliced thin (3 to 4 very large)

prose.intro_html: A Philly cheesesteak is one of the great sandwiches, and the only thing standing between it and a clean meal-prep dinner is the roll. So we lose the roll. Thin shaved beef, onions and mushrooms cooked all the way down soft, piled into a roasted bell pepper and capped with a slice of melting provolone. You get every part of the cheesesteak you actually came for, the beef and the cheese and the sweet onion, and none of the bread that runs up the carbs. Built at 14 servings it lands around {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 20 grams of carbs. That is a steak-and-cheese dinner that works with your macros instead of against them.
shop_smart: Three pounds of shaved beef steak is the anchor. This is the thin sliced beef sold in trays in the meat case, the same cut that builds a real cheesesteak. If your store does not stock it, buy a sirloin steak, freeze it for about 20 minutes until it is firm, and slice it as thin as you can against the grain. This is where the protein in every serving comes from.

Seven green bell peppers are the bowls. Each one gets halved and seeded, which gives you fourteen boats, one per serving. Pick peppers that are firm and sit fairly flat so they hold the filling without tipping over.

Three and a half pounds of onions and close to two pounds of mushrooms do the heavy lifting. They cook all the way down into the soft, sweet, savory filling that makes a cheesesteak taste like a cheesesteak, and they stretch three pounds of beef across fourteen full servings. Both are cheap staples you can always use.
Fourteen slices of provolone finish it. One slice melted over each stuffed pepper. Deli sliced provolone from the cheese case is all you need.

Butter, vegetable oil, Worcestershire, garlic powder, salt and pepper are the seasoning. The butter and oil caramelize the onions and mushrooms and brown the beef, and the Worcestershire and garlic powder give the filling that deep, meaty savor. These are backbone items you cook with all the time.
make_it: Weigh your biggest skillet empty and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split the filling evenly across all fourteen peppers instead of guessing.

Heat the oven to 350 degrees. Halve the bell peppers the long way and pull out the seeds and ribs. Brush the cut sides with a little of the vegetable oil and a pinch of the salt and pepper, set them cut side up on a sheet pan, and bake for 25 minutes to soften them while you build the filling.

Melt about half the butter with a couple spoons of the oil in the skillet over medium high heat. Add the sliced onions and a pinch of the salt and cook them down until they are very soft and starting to caramelize, about 10 minutes.

Add the sliced mushrooms, the garlic powder, the rest of the salt and pepper, and the Worcestershire sauce. Keep cooking until the mushrooms are soft and the liquid has cooked off, about 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits as you go. Turn the heat down if things start to scorch.

Push the vegetables to the side of the pan, add the rest of the butter and oil, and lay in the shaved beef. Break it apart with your spatula as it cooks so it browns evenly, then stir it together with the onions and mushrooms.
Weigh the full skillet, subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1, and divide the filling by 14. Mound that amount into each roasted pepper half. They should be very full.
Lay a slice of provolone over each stuffed pepper and return them to the oven for about 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Portion into your containers and you are done.
prose.portion_html: The honest way to make fourteen even servings is by weight. Weigh the loaded skillet, subtract the empty weight from Step 1, and that is your total filling. Divide it by 14 and spoon that exact amount into each pepper half before the cheese goes on. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving at everyday prices for a cheesesteak dinner you can eat all week. The peppers, onions and mushrooms stretch three pounds of beef into fourteen full plates.

head.keywords: philly cheesesteak stuffed peppers, low carb cheesesteak, shaved beef meal prep, stuffed bell peppers, high protein low carb dinner
steps: Halve and seed the bell peppers, brush with oil, and bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes to soften.
Caramelize the sliced onions in butter and oil, then add the mushrooms, garlic powder, Worcestershire, salt and pepper and cook until soft.
Add the rest of the butter and oil and brown the shaved beef, then stir it into the vegetables.
Weigh the skillet, subtract the empty weight, and divide the filling across fourteen roasted pepper halves.
Top each with a slice of provolone and bake 20 minutes until melted, then portion into containers.
